messages.content: אני רוצה לדעת את תחזית המזג אוויר לתל אביב. בוא נבדוק את זה עבור קווי רוחב וקו אורך.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
The user wants the weather forecast for Tel Aviv. They want to check using latitude and longitude. We need to call the Open-Meteo API. We need to find the coordinates for Tel Aviv. Tel Aviv is approximately at latitude 32.0853° N, longitude 34.7818° E. So we can use those coordinates.

We need to call the function requests_get with appropriate parameters. The function signature expects:

- url: string
- headers?: { Content-Type?: string, Accept?: string }
- timeout?: number
- params: { latitude?: number, longitude?: number, elevation?: number }
- allow_redirects?: boolean
- auth?: string[]
- cert?: string
- cookies?: { sessionid?: string, csrftoken?: string }
- proxies?: { http?: string, https?: string }
- stream?: boolean
- verify?: boolean

We need to provide the URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint. For weather forecast, we can use "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". Then we need to pass query parameters: latitude=32.0853, longitude=34.7818, maybe also specify hourly or daily variables. But the user just wants the forecast. We can ask for daily summary: temperature_2m_max, temperature_2m_min, precipitation_sum, windspeed_10m_max, etc. But the user didn't specify. We can just get the daily forecast for the next few days.

Let's choose daily variables: temperature_2m_max, temperature_2m_min, precipitation_sum, windspeed_10m_max, windgust_10m_max, sunrise, sunset. And we can set timezone=Asia/Jerusalem. Also we can set start_date and end_date. But we can just let the API return the default.

So we will call the function with:

url: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast"
params: {
  latitude: 32.0853,
  longitude: 34.7818,
  daily: "temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,windspeed_10m_max,windgust_10m_max,sunrise,sunset",
  timezone: "Asia/Jerusalem"
}

We don't need to set other optional fields.

Thus we call the function.
